verses.text: Jerusalem, the city that was once so full of people, is now empty and deserted. It was once the greatest city among all the nations, but now it is like a widow—alone and without protection. It was once honored among the provinces like a princess, but now her people are forced to do slave labor.
verses.heading: ALEPH

verses.text: Jerusalem’s inhabitants weep and cry bitterly all through the night; tears run down their cheeks. None of the nations that loved them have come to comfort them. All their allies have turned against them; they have all become their enemies.
verses.heading: BETH

verses.text: Enemies drove the people of Judah out to other countries, and made them suffer greatly as slaves. They live among foreign nations, where they find no peace or rest. Their enemies caught up with them; they were trapped and could not escape.
verses.heading: GIMEL

verses.text: No one comes to Zion anymore for the sacred festivals, so the roads to the city are silent and empty. The city gates stand deserted; the priests groan in sorrow. The young women of the city are grieving, and the whole city is filled with bitterness.
verses.heading: DALETH

verses.text: Jerusalem’s enemies have become rulers over it; its adversaries are doing well. Yahweh has caused it to suffer greatly, because of all the ways its people sinned against him. Its children have been taken captive and marched away before the enemy.
verses.heading: HE

verses.text: All the glory and beauty that Zion once had has left it completely. Its leaders are like deer that are starving because they cannot find any grass to eat. They stumble along weakly with the enemy chasing them.
verses.heading: WAW

verses.text: Now as Jerusalem suffers in exile and misery, its people remember all the good things that they had in former times. When the enemy conquered the people, no one came to help them. Some enemies watched and laughed contemptuously as others destroyed the city.
verses.heading: ZAYIN

verses.text: Jerusalem’s people sinned so greatly that the city became something everyone treated as filthy and defiling. All those who had honored it now despise it, because they have seen how shamefully disgraced it has become. Now its people moan and humbly hide.
verses.heading: HETH

verses.text: Everyone can see that the people in Jerusalem have made themselves impure by sinning, but its people never thought about what would happen to them as a result. The enemy devastated Jerusalem in a terrible way; no one has come to comfort its people. They cried out, “Yahweh, see how we are suffering! The enemy has triumphed over us!”
verses.heading: TETH

verses.text: The enemy took possession of all its precious treasures. Its people watched as foreign nations entered the temple— the nations that you, Yahweh, had commanded to stay out of your holy place.
verses.heading: YODH

verses.text: All the people groan and search for food. They have traded their precious things just to get something to eat so that they can stay alive. They cried out, “Yahweh, look at us! See how people treat us contemptuously!”
verses.heading: KAPH

verses.text: Jerusalem’s people cried out to those passing by the ruined city, “Do you not care at all about what has happened to us? Look around you and see— has anyone ever suffered as much as we have suffered? Yahweh inflicted this terrible pain on us on the day when he was fiercely angry.
verses.heading: LAMEDH

verses.text: He sent fire down from above that burned deep inside us. He set a trap that caught our feet and forced us to turn back. He left us devastated and abandoned, exhausted and miserable all day long.
verses.heading: MEM

verses.text: God tied our sins around our necks like a heavy yoke; they are twisted tightly together so that we cannot remove them. They are piled onto our necks and weigh us down, so that we have no strength left. The Lord handed us over to enemies we have no power to defeat.
verses.heading: NUN

verses.text: The Lord has despised and rejected all our warriors. He called our enemies together at the right time to destroy our young men. The Lord has crushed the people of Judah like someone treading on grapes in a winepress.
verses.heading: SAMEKH

verses.text: These are the things we weep over, weeping without stopping; our eyes overflow with tears. There is no one near us to comfort us or to restore our strength. Our children have been left with nothing, because the enemy has overcome us.”
verses.heading: AYIN

verses.text: Zion’s people reach out their hands, pleading for help, but no one comes to comfort them. Yahweh ordered that all the nations surrounding Jacob would become his enemies. Jerusalem has become something all the neighboring nations treat as defiling and avoid.
verses.heading: PE

verses.text: Jerusalem’s people said, “Yahweh is righteous, because we disobeyed his commands. Listen, all you peoples of the world, and see what great pain we are in. Our young women and young men have been taken away as captives.
verses.heading: TSADHE

verses.text: We called to our allies for help, but they completely betrayed us. Our priests and our elders died in the city, while they were desperately searching for food just to stay alive.
verses.heading: QOPH

verses.text: Yahweh, look at how much we are suffering! Our stomachs churn with anguish; our hearts are completely devastated within us, because we have deeply and truly rebelled against you. In the streets, the sword kills people; inside the city, people are dying like a plague.
verses.heading: RESH

verses.text: People have heard us groaning in misery, but no one has come to comfort us. All our enemies have heard about the disaster that came upon us; they are glad about it, because you are the one who brought it. Bring the day of punishment that you promised, when they will suffer as we have suffered!
verses.heading: SIN

verses.text: Let all the evil things they have done come to your attention, and punish them for what they have done. Treat them the way you treated us for all the ways we sinned against you. We are constantly sighing and groaning, and we grieve greatly.”
verses.heading: TAW

verses.text: The Lord was very angry with the people of Jerusalem, so he brought darkness and judgment on them. Jerusalem used to be a beautiful and glorious city, but he humiliated it and brought it down to nothing. When the day came for him to punish Israel, he did not even spare his own temple.
verses.heading: ALEPH

verses.text: The Lord completely destroyed all the homes of Jacob’s descendants and was not merciful to them. Because he was furious, he tore the fortresses of the people of Judah down to the ground. He disgraced their kingdom and its rulers.
verses.heading: BETH

verses.text: Because he was extremely angry, he took away all of Israel’s power. He refused to protect his people when their enemies attacked them. He destroyed everything among Jacob’s descendants like a raging fire that burns up everything around it.
verses.heading: GIMEL

verses.text: He got ready to shoot his bow at us, his own people, as though we were his enemies. He used his power to kill everyone we loved most among the people of Jerusalem. He was extremely angry with us; his anger burned like a fire.
verses.heading: DALETH

verses.text: The Lord started treating us like an enemy; he destroyed Israel. He destroyed all of Jerusalem’s palaces and turned its fortresses into ruins. He caused the people of Judah to grieve and weep even more.
verses.heading: HE

verses.text: He wrecked his own temple as easily as someone tears down a garden hut; he destroyed the place where people gathered to worship him. Yahweh caused the people of Zion to stop celebrating their sacred festivals and Sabbath days. Because he was so furiously angry, he rejected both the king and the priest.
verses.heading: WAW

verses.text: The Lord turned away from his own altar; he abandoned his own holy place. He let the enemies have power over the walls of Jerusalem’s palaces. Those enemies shouted triumphantly inside Yahweh’s temple, as if they were celebrating one of the sacred festivals.
verses.heading: ZAYIN

verses.text: Yahweh planned to destroy the wall of Jerusalem. He carefully measured it out for destruction and then he did not stop himself from devouring it. He made the outer wall and the inner wall fall into ruin; together they crumbled.
verses.heading: HETH

verses.text: Jerusalem’s gates have sunk into the ground; Yahweh smashed the bars that held them shut. The enemy has taken the king and the officials away to foreign nations; no one teaches them God’s instruction anymore. The prophets also no longer receive any messages from Yahweh.
verses.heading: TETH

verses.text: The old men of Jerusalem sit on the ground and say nothing. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on rough sackcloth {to show how deeply they grieve}. The young women of Jerusalem bow their faces all the way down to the ground.
verses.heading: YODH

verses.text: I have cried until my eyes can produce no more tears; my stomach is churning with anguish. I feel as if my insides are spilling out on the ground, because so many of my people have died. Even children and babies are fainting in the city streets because they have nothing to eat.
verses.heading: KAPH

verses.text: The children cry out to their mothers, “We need food and drink!” They collapse in the city streets like fatally wounded soldiers, and they die slowly in the arms of their mothers.
verses.heading: LAMEDH

verses.text: People of Jerusalem, there is nothing I can say to help you. Nothing that has ever happened to anyone else compares to what has happened to you people who live on mount Zion; I do not know how to comfort you. The disaster that struck you is as vast as the sea; no one can restore you.
verses.heading: MEM

verses.text: The prophets among you claimed to hear messages from Yahweh, but what they said was false and worthless. They did not rebuke you when you sinned so that you could have changed your ways and avoided disaster. Instead, the messages they told you were lies that caused you to do wrong things.
verses.heading: NUN

verses.text: Everyone who passes by on the road claps their hands to mock you. They hiss with contempt and shake their heads at Jerusalem: “Can this really be the city that people used to say was the perfectly beautiful city, the city that made all the earth rejoice?”
verses.heading: SAMEKH

verses.text: All your enemies open their mouths wide against you to mock you. They hiss with contempt and grind their teeth with hatred; they say, “We have devoured her! This is the very day we waited for; we have lived to see it!”
verses.heading: AYIN

verses.text: Yahweh has done what he planned to do; he has carried out the threat that he announced long ago. He has torn the city down and shown no mercy; he has let your enemies celebrate over you, and he has made those who attack you more powerful than ever.
verses.heading: PE

verses.text: The people of Jerusalem cried out to the Lord from deep within themselves. People of Jerusalem, let your tears flow like a river all day and all night! Do not stop weeping; do not let your eyes rest from crying.
verses.heading: TSADHE

verses.text: Get up and cry out during the night, right when the night watches begin! Tell the Lord everything that is in your heart, holding nothing back, like water pouring out. Raise your hands and pray to him for your children to survive, because they are fainting from hunger on every street corner.
verses.heading: QOPH

verses.text: Yahweh, look at what you have done and pay attention! Think about whom you have treated this way! Women should never have to eat their own children, the babies they lovingly cared for! No one should kill priests and prophets inside your own holy place!
verses.heading: RESH

verses.text: People of every age lie dead on the ground in the streets. The enemy has killed all our youth. On the day you were angry, you {let the enemy} kill them; you let them slaughter them mercilessly.
verses.heading: SIN

verses.text: You called enemies to attack me from every direction, as if you were summoning guests to come to a feast. On the day Yahweh was angry, no one escaped and no one survived. The children I carried and raised, my enemy has destroyed them all.
verses.heading: TAW

verses.text: I am a man who has suffered greatly because God punished me when he was very angry.
verses.heading: ALEPH

verses.text: He sent me into a place where I only suffer and nothing good happens to me.
He keeps acting against me again and again, all day long.
He afflicted my body and broke my bones.
verses.heading: BETH

verses.text: He attacked me on every side and caused me to suffer terribly.
He made me feel hopeless, like no one remembers me.
He has completely trapped me so that I cannot escape.
verses.heading: GIMEL

verses.text: Even though I beg him to help me, he refuses to listen when I pray.
He has blocked every way forward for me so that I cannot make any progress in my life.
He waited to attack me like a bear hiding to ambush its prey, like a lion crouching in a hidden place.
verses.heading: DALETH

verses.text: He ruined my plans and destroyed me; he made me poor.
He deliberately chose to attack me and made me the one he would harm.
He deliberately caused me intense suffering.
verses.heading: HE

verses.text: All my own people mock me constantly with their songs.
He has caused me to suffer so much that I cannot bear it.
He completely humiliated me and degraded me.
verses.heading: WAW

verses.text: God took away all my peace; I no longer remember what happiness feels like.
So I said to myself, “I cannot endure any longer, and I have no more reason to hope in Yahweh.”
Yahweh, remember how I have suffered and wandered; I have suffered so very greatly.
verses.heading: ZAYIN

verses.text: I keep thinking about it over and over, and it makes me deeply depressed.
Yet when I think about this one thing, I find reason to hope:
Yahweh never stops faithfully loving us, and he never stops showing us mercy.
verses.heading: HETH

verses.text: Every morning he shows us mercy again; he is always faithful to us.
I said to myself, “Yahweh is all that I need; so I will confidently wait for him.”
Yahweh is good to everyone who depends on him, to everyone who hopes that Yahweh will help him.
verses.heading: TETH

verses.text: It is good to wait quietly for Yahweh to save us.
It is good for a person to endure suffering patiently while still young.
A person should accept his situation quietly and not complain when God causes him to suffer.
verses.heading: YODH

verses.text: He should bow down with his face to the ground, because there may still be reason to hope.
He should offer his cheek to the one who hits him and accept all the insults people give him.
The Lord does not reject people forever.
verses.heading: KAPH

verses.text: Even though he causes people to grieve, he will show them mercy because he always faithfully loves them.
He does not enjoy causing people to suffer or making them grieve.
When people crush all the prisoners in a land under their feet,
verses.heading: LAMEDH

verses.text: when they cheat someone and deny him what he deserves right in front of the Most High God,
when they treat someone unfairly in his legal dispute—the Lord does not approve of any of these things.
No one can simply speak and make something happen unless the Lord has commanded it.
verses.heading: MEM

verses.text: The Most High God is the one who decides both the bad things and the good things that happen.
No living person should complain when God punishes him for his sins.
Instead, we should carefully examine how we have been living, and we should turn back to Yahweh.
verses.heading: NUN

verses.text: We should sincerely pray, raising our hands to God in heaven:
“We have sinned and rebelled against you, and you have not forgiven us.
Because you were angry, you chased after us; you killed us without showing us any mercy.
verses.heading: SAMEKH

verses.text: You made yourself unreachable so that you did not hear any of our prayers.
You have made the other nations treat us as though we are nothing but garbage and filth.
All our enemies have spoken hateful things against us.
verses.heading: AYIN

verses.text: We have experienced nothing but fear and danger, ruin and destruction.”
Many tears flow from my eyes because enemies have destroyed my people.
My tears pour out and will not stop; they will not end
verses.heading: PE

verses.text: until Yahweh looks down and sees us from heaven.
What I see makes me grieve deeply because of what has happened to all the women of my city.
My enemies relentlessly pursued me without any reason, even though I had done nothing wrong.
verses.heading: TSADHE

verses.text: They threw me into a pit to kill me and dropped stones on top of me.
Water rose over my head, and I said to myself, “I am going to die!”
I called out to you, Yahweh, from the deepest part of that pit.
verses.heading: QOPH

verses.text: You heard me; do not ignore me when I cry out to you for help!
You came near when I called to you and said, “Do not be afraid!”
Lord, you defended me; you saved my life.
verses.heading: RESH

verses.text: Yahweh, you have seen how my enemies have wronged me; make things right for me!
You have seen how they want to take revenge on me and all the things they have planned to do to me.
Yahweh, you have heard them insult me and all the things they have planned to do to me.
verses.heading: SIN

verses.text: Those who oppose me whisper and mutter things about me all day long.
Look at them! No matter what they are doing, they make fun of me in their songs.
Yahweh, pay them back for what they have done!
verses.heading: TAW

verses.text: Make them stubborn, and let your curse fall on them.
Because you are angry with them, chase them and destroy them so they no longer exist anywhere on earth.
How terrible that the people of Jerusalem, who used to be so valuable, have now become completely worthless! The enemy has thrown out the precious young men at every street corner.
verses.heading: ALEPH

verses.text: People once considered the young men of Zion to be extremely valuable, but now everyone treats them as completely worthless, like ordinary clay pots that a potter makes.
verses.heading: BETH

verses.text: Even jackals nurse their young, but the women among my people have neglected their own children and have stopped caring for them.
verses.heading: GIMEL

verses.text: The babies are so thirsty that their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths. The children beg for food, but no one gives them any.
verses.heading: DALETH

verses.text: People who used to eat the finest food now starve in the streets. People whose parents raised them wearing expensive clothes now search through garbage heaps for something to eat.
verses.heading: HE

verses.text: God has punished my people more severely than he punished the people of Sodom. He destroyed Sodom in an instant, and nobody cried for it.
verses.heading: WAW

verses.text: Jerusalem’s most honored people used to look very pure and healthy. They had strong, attractive bodies and appeared very vigorous.
verses.heading: ZAYIN

verses.text: But now they look so dark and thin that no one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin has shriveled tightly over their bones and has dried out completely.
verses.heading: HETH

verses.text: Those who died quickly in battle were better off than those who died slowly from starvation, because the starving people wasted away gradually since no food grew in the fields.
verses.heading: TETH

verses.text: Women who were normally very compassionate cooked their own children. They ate them as food when the enemy destroyed Jerusalem.
verses.heading: YODH

verses.text: Yahweh expressed all of his anger against Jerusalem. He burned the city with fire and destroyed it down to its very foundations.
verses.heading: KAPH

verses.text: No king anywhere on the earth, and no one else in the whole world, believed that an enemy could ever enter the city of Jerusalem.
verses.heading: LAMEDH

verses.text: But it happened because Jerusalem’s prophets sinned and her priests did evil things. They killed innocent people right there in the city.
verses.heading: MEM

verses.text: Those prophets and priests wandered through the streets, confused and unable to find their way. The blood of the people they had killed made them so unclean that no one would touch even their clothes.
verses.heading: NUN

verses.text: People shouted at them, “Go away! You are unclean! Do not touch us!” So those priests and prophets fled and wandered from place to place, but even the people in other nations said, “They cannot stay here.”
verses.heading: SAMEKH

verses.text: Yahweh himself scattered them and no longer watches over them. People in those nations do not respect our priests and do not show any kindness to our elders.
verses.heading: AYIN

verses.text: We kept watching and waiting for a nation to come and help us, but no help ever came. The nation we hoped would rescue us could not save us.
verses.heading: PE

verses.text: Our enemies tracked us so closely that we could not even walk through our own city squares. The time for our destruction was near, and our final days had come.
verses.heading: TSADHE

verses.text: Those who chased us were extremely fast. They pursued us over the mountains and ambushed us in the desert.
verses.heading: QOPH

verses.text: Our enemies captured the king whom Yahweh had chosen to lead us, the one who kept us alive. We had said about him, “He will protect us even if we have to live among other nations.”
verses.heading: RESH

verses.text: The people of Edom who live in the land of Uz may be happy now about what has happened to Jerusalem, but Yahweh will punish them too. He will cause them to suffer greatly and be completely humiliated.
verses.heading: SIN

verses.text: Yahweh will finish punishing the people of Jerusalem, and he will not keep them in exile any longer. However, he will punish the people of Edom and expose all the evil things they have done.
verses.heading: TAW

verses.text: Yahweh, think about what has happened to us. Pay attention and see how people have disgraced us.
verses.heading: A prayer for God’s mercy

verses.text: Our enemies have taken our property and given it to people we do not know; they have seized our homes and given them to people who are not Israelites.
We have no fathers to care for us; our mothers have no husbands.
We have to pay money to drink our own water, and we have to buy the wood that we need.
Our enemies chase us and never let up; we are exhausted, but they do not let us rest.
We surrendered to Egypt and Assyria so that we could get enough food to survive.
Our ancestors sinned and then they died, but we are the ones suffering for what they did wrong.
People who used to be slaves now rule over us, and no one can rescue us from their power.
We risk our lives when we go out to get food, because violent people in the wilderness will kill us.
Our skin burns with fever because we are starving so badly.
Our enemies raped women in Zion and young women in the towns of Judah.
Our enemies hung our leaders by their hands; they did not respect our elders.
They forced our young men to grind flour with millstones, and boys staggered under heavy loads of firewood.
Our elders no longer gather to make decisions, and our young men no longer play music.
We no longer feel happy; instead of dancing, we grieve.
We have lost the honor that we once had. How terrible it is for us, because we have sinned!
Because of all this, we feel sick inside; because of these things, we cannot stop crying.
We are sad because Mount Zion lies empty with no one living there; foxes roam through it.
But you, Yahweh, rule forever! You have authority over every generation.
It feels as though you have forgotten us completely and abandoned us for such a long time.
Yahweh, please bring us back to yourself so that we may return; make our lives as good as they were before.
Please do not completely reject us or stay extremely angry with us forever!
